description: How to pin Gmail to Dock on Mac: add it from Safari or Chrome, with exact menu paths, Dock tips and fixes for common problems.

intro: Open mail.google.com in Safari, choose File > Add to Dock, type Gmail, and click Add. In Chrome, choose More (three dots) > Cast, save, and share > Install page as app instead.
tldr: Gmail has no standalone Mac app from Google in the sources checked, so the Dock icon is a web app.
In Safari, choose File > Add to Dock. This route needs macOS Sonoma 14 or later.
In Chrome, choose More (three dots) > Cast, save, and share > Install page as app.
If the icon is missing from the Dock, drag the app from Applications onto the Dock.

blocks.text: What pinning Gmail to the Dock actually does

Google does not publish a standalone Gmail app for Mac in the sources checked for this page. Pinning Gmail to the Dock means saving a web app. It is a Gmail window with its own icon. Apple says the Safari version has a simplified toolbar instead of the full browser controls, so it looks more like an app than a tab. Your mail still lives on Google's servers, the same as it does in a regular browser tab.

Safari and Chrome can both create these web apps, and the steps differ between them. Safari's version comes from Apple's help pages. Chrome's version comes from Google's. In both cases the result is the same. You get an icon in the Dock that opens mail.google.com in its own window, and you do not need a third-party app to do it.
Check your macOS version before you start

Apple's help page on Safari web apps says the feature requires macOS Sonoma 14 or later. To see your version, click the Apple menu, then choose About This Mac. The version appears near the top of the window. If you are on an older release, skip the Safari route and use Chrome.

Google's Chrome help page does not list a macOS minimum or a Chrome version for its install steps. If Chrome opens Gmail on your Mac, check the menu first, then look for the install icon in the address bar.
Option 1: pin Gmail to the Dock from Safari

Safari is the shortest route. Open mail.google.com, sign in, and wait until your inbox loads. Then choose File > Add to Dock from the menu bar. You can also click the Share button in the Safari toolbar and choose Add to Dock. Apple's guide lists both paths, and both open the same prompt.

The prompt asks for a name. Type Gmail, or a name that tells accounts apart, such as Gmail work. Then click Add. Apple says the web app is saved in the Applications folder in your home folder. You can open it from the Dock or from Spotlight. Apple's pages list no other options in this prompt.

Apple also says a signed-in Safari session usually carries over to the web app. In most cases, you will not need to sign in a second time. If the web app asks you to sign in, use the same Google account you use in Safari, so the inbox matches what you expect.
Option 2: add Gmail to the Dock from Chrome

Chrome takes a few more clicks. Open Chrome, go to mail.google.com, and sign in. Click More, the three dots at the top right. Choose Cast, save, and share, then choose Install page as app. Google's help page says to follow the on-screen instructions to finish the install. Each prompt asks you to confirm, so read it before you click.

On some sites, Chrome shows an Install icon at the top right of the address bar instead of the menu item. If you see it, click it and skip the menu. Labels can shift between Chrome releases, so look for the word Install and check that the prompt names Gmail before you confirm.
Keep the Gmail icon in the Dock

After a Safari install, Apple says the icon appears in the Dock and in Applications. If you installed through Chrome, check the Dock first. If the icon is missing, open Applications in the Finder, find the Gmail app, and drag it onto the Dock. Drop it on the left side of the thin divider line, where app icons go.

Some third-party guides describe a right-click menu on the Dock icon with Options > Keep in Dock. Apple's and Google's pages did not confirm that option, so use it only if your Mac shows it. Dragging the app from Applications works either way.
Make a second shortcut from Chrome's apps page

If you installed Gmail in Chrome and want another shortcut in a different place, use the apps page. Type chrome://apps in a new tab. Right-click the Gmail icon, choose Create shortcut, pick where it should appear, and click Create. Google's help page describes this method for Windows, Mac, and Linux.
How the pinned Gmail window behaves

The pinned window has a simplified toolbar, so you see less browser chrome than in a normal tab. Apple says the web app can send notifications. Open System Settings > Notifications, find Gmail in the list, and choose how alerts appear. If you turn them off, new mail will still be waiting in the inbox.

Neither Apple nor Google's pages listed keyboard shortcuts for pinning, so this guide does not give any. Gmail's own keyboard shortcuts are a separate setting inside Gmail. The guide on [turning on keyboard shortcuts in Gmail](/how-to/turn-on-keyboard-shortcuts-in-gmail) walks through that setting for your browser.
Common mistakes that stop the pin from working

The first mistake is searching the Mac App Store. The pin route does not use the App Store. It makes a web app from the page you already have open, so the page must finish loading first. A blank sign in page makes a poor app.

The second mistake is pinning the wrong account. The web app carries the session you sign in with. If you use two Google accounts, sign in with the one you want before you pin, and give each app a clear name such as Gmail work and Gmail personal.
The third mistake is skipping the version check. The Safari option needs macOS Sonoma 14 or later. Check About This Mac before you hunt through menus, so you know which route your Mac can use.
Safari or Chrome: which route fits your Mac?

Pick Safari if you already work in Safari and run macOS Sonoma 14 or later. The menu path is short, and Apple's guide describes the result clearly. Pick Chrome if your work already lives in Chrome, or if the Safari option is missing on your version of macOS.

Think about where you are signed in. If your Google account is signed in only in Chrome, the Safari web app may ask you to sign in again. That is not a fault. Safari is a separate browser with its own sessions.
Why one click to Gmail matters for daily mail

Google says 3 billion people use Gmail, according to its January 8, 2026 blog post. That scale means many people reach their inbox through a browser tab every day. A Dock icon gives you one click instead of a hunt through open tabs, and it keeps mail separate from your other browsing.
Removing the Gmail app from the Dock on a Mac

To remove the web app, choose Go > Home in the Finder, open Applications, and drag the Gmail web app to the Trash. Apple's guide lists this removal path. Removing the app takes away the Dock shortcut and the window. Your Google account and your mail stay where they are.
Next steps after your Gmail icon is in the Dock

Once Gmail has its own icon, a few settings save the most time. [Filters](/how-to/create-a-filter-in-gmail) sort incoming mail before you see it. [Labels](/how-to/create-a-label-in-gmail) group messages by project. Both have their own how-to pages, with steps for Safari and Chrome.
Start with one filter and one label. Use them for a week, then add more. A small setup you keep is more useful than a long list you forget.

faq.question: Is there an official Gmail app for Mac?
faq.answer: The sources checked for this page do not show a standalone Gmail app from Google for Mac. The Dock icon in this guide is a web app that Safari or Chrome creates from mail.google.com. Both routes use that same page.

faq.question: Does pinning Gmail to the Dock need macOS Sonoma 14?
faq.answer: Apple's help page for Safari web apps says the feature requires macOS Sonoma 14 or later. Google's Chrome help page does not list a macOS version for its install steps. On an older Mac, check the Chrome route first.

faq.question: Why don't I see Add to Dock in Safari?
faq.answer: Make sure the Gmail page is open and fully loaded. Then check the File menu and the Share button in the toolbar. If neither shows Add to Dock, confirm your macOS version. The troubleshooting list covers the other cases.

faq.question: Can I pin Gmail without Safari or Chrome?
faq.answer: The routes in this guide use Safari or Chrome, since both create web apps from a page. The sources checked do not describe a method for other browsers, so this guide sticks to these two.

faq.question: Will the pinned Gmail stay signed in?
faq.answer: Apple says a signed-in Safari session usually carries over to the web app. Google's help page does not say the same about Chrome installs. If the app asks you to sign in, use the account you use every day.

faq.question: Can I pin two Gmail accounts?
faq.answer: In Safari, repeat the steps with a different name for each account, such as Gmail work and Gmail personal. Chrome may install only one app per site, and the sources checked do not say how it handles two accounts. Use Safari for the second one if Chrome refuses.

faq.question: How do I remove Gmail from the Dock?
faq.answer: Remove the web app itself. Choose Go > Home in the Finder, open Applications, and drag the Gmail web app to the Trash. This step does not delete your Google account or your mail.

task: Pin Gmail to the Dock on a Mac
appliesTo: Gmail in Safari on macOS Sonoma 14 or later, or Chrome on a Mac
requirements: A Mac running macOS Sonoma 14 or later for the Safari route
Safari or Google Chrome installed on your Mac
A Google account that can sign in to Gmail
Finder access to your Applications folder
An internet connection while you sign in

steps.name: Check your macOS version
steps.text: Click the Apple menu, then choose About This Mac. Apple's Safari web app help page says the feature requires macOS Sonoma 14 or later.
steps.tip: On an older version, skip the Safari steps and use the Chrome steps below.

steps.name: Open Gmail in Safari
steps.text: Open Safari, go to mail.google.com, and sign in. Wait until your inbox loads completely before you add it to the Dock.
steps.tip: The web app saves the page you have open, so a blank sign in page makes a poor app.

steps.name: Choose Add to Dock from the File menu
steps.text: With the Gmail page active, click File in the menu bar, then choose Add to Dock.

steps.name: Or use the Share button
steps.text: Click the Share button in the Safari toolbar, then choose Add to Dock. Both paths open the same prompt.

steps.name: Name the web app
steps.text: In the prompt, type Gmail, or a name that tells accounts apart, such as Gmail work. Apple's pages list no other options in this prompt.
steps.tip: Pick a name you will recognize in Spotlight, too.

steps.name: Click Add
steps.text: Click Add. Apple says the web app is saved in the Applications folder in your home folder, and its icon appears in the Dock.

steps.name: Open the web app to check it
steps.text: Click the new icon in the Dock, or open it from Spotlight. Gmail should open in its own window with a simplified toolbar.

steps.name: Open Gmail in Chrome
steps.text: Open Chrome, go to mail.google.com, and sign in. Click More, the three dots at the top right of the window.

steps.name: Choose Install page as app
steps.text: Choose Cast, save, and share, then choose Install page as app. Follow the on-screen instructions to finish the install.

steps.name: Use the address bar icon if it appears
steps.text: On some sites, an Install icon appears at the top right of the address bar instead. Click it, then follow the prompts to finish.
steps.tip: Check that the prompt names Gmail before you confirm.

steps.name: Confirm the Gmail icon is in the Dock
steps.text: Look for Gmail in the Dock. If it is missing, choose Go > Home in the Finder, open Applications, and drag the Gmail app onto the left side of the Dock divider.

steps.name: Make a second Chrome shortcut
steps.text: Type chrome://apps in a new tab. Right-click the Gmail icon, choose Create shortcut, pick where it should appear, and click Create.

steps.name: Remove the web app later
steps.text: Choose Go > Home in the Finder, open Applications, and drag the Gmail web app to the Trash.

troubleshooting.problem: Add to Dock does not appear in the File menu.
troubleshooting.fix: Make sure the Gmail page is active and has finished loading. Then confirm your Mac runs macOS Sonoma 14 or later, which Apple lists as the requirement.

troubleshooting.problem: The Install page as app option is missing in Chrome.
troubleshooting.fix: Look for the Install icon at the top right of the address bar. Google's help page does not explain missing options. If Chrome is managed by a work or school account, ask your IT team.

troubleshooting.problem: The Gmail icon is not in the Dock.
troubleshooting.fix: Open Applications from the Finder, then drag the Gmail app onto the left side of the Dock divider. Apple says the web app is saved there.

troubleshooting.problem: Gmail asks you to sign in again.
troubleshooting.fix: Apple says a signed-in Safari session usually carries over. Sign in with the account you use every day. If the wrong account opens, sign out in the web app and sign in again.

troubleshooting.problem: Gmail notifications do not show up.
troubleshooting.fix: Open System Settings > Notifications, find Gmail in the list, and turn on alerts. Apple says the web app can send notifications.

troubleshooting.problem: You want to pin a second Gmail account.
troubleshooting.fix: Repeat the Safari steps with a different name. If Chrome refuses a second install for the same site, use Safari for the second account.
